items.quote: Penn named the city Philadelphia, which is Greek for 'brotherly love'
items.note: Very well known (City of Brotherly Love), but unambiguous.

items.quote: the Liberty Bell today is located across the street from Independence Hall in the Liberty Bell Center
the Declaration of Independence was adopted there on July 4, 1776
including the statue of city founder William Penn atop its tower
items.note: Mild giveaway: 'founder of Pennsylvania' points hard at Penn. Acceptable for a family round.

items.quote: The Rocky Steps is an informal name to the 72 stone steps leading up to the East entrance of the Philadelphia Museum of Art in Philadelphia that gained global fame after being featured in a notable scene from the 1976 film Rocky
items.note: Rewording fixed it: the answer now carries both names, and the October 2025 rebrand to 'Philadelphia Art Museum' is in en:Philadelphia_Museum_of_Art. 'Front steps' is the east entrance, the only steps he runs. Accept 'the Art Museum' / 'the Rocky Steps' building.

items.quote: A cheesesteak (also known as a Philadelphia cheesesteak, Philly cheesesteak, cheesesteak sandwich, cheese steak, or steak and cheese) is a sandwich made from thinly sliced pieces of beefsteak
items.note: Same article: 'American cheese, provolone, and Cheez Whiz are the most commonly used cheeses'. A hoagie is a different sandwich, so no second answer.

items.quote: The Mummers Parade is held each New Year's Day in Philadelphia
The underdog Eagles defeated the Patriots with a score of 41–33 to win their first Super Bowl
items.note: The Eagles have since won a second (Super Bowl LIX, Feb 2025, over Kansas City), so the question must keep both 'first' and 'February 2018'; it does.

items.quote: Benjamin Franklin Bridge crosses the Delaware, connecting Philadelphia and Camden, New Jersey
Boathouse Row is row of fifteen boathouses on the east bank of the Schuylkill River in Philadelphia
items.note: Lights: 'In 1979, lights ... were installed to outline each of the boathouses'.
